item.title: The importance of shear strain in narrow Si/SiGe quantum wells
item.description: arXiv:2611.16015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Several heterostructure profiles have been proposed for Si/SiGe quantum wells, to improve the operation of quantum-dot spin qubits. These structures share a common goal of generating either of the two wave vectors that govern the conduction-band valley coupling, dubbed $k_0$ and $k_1$. Here, we focus on the long-wavelength $k_1$ term that couples valleys when paired with shear strain, and which governs the Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling. We show that shear strain induced by metal top gates may be enough to activate the $k_1$ valley-coupling mechanism, mitigating the need for "ultrasharp" interfaces, as commonly assumed for large valley energy splittings. We propose a scheme featuring narrow quantum wells that does not require ultrasharp interfaces, but should still provide large deterministic valley splittings (when paired with shear strain), and large spin-orbit couplings and $g$-factor corrections, which are of great interest for experimental implementations.
item.dc:creator: Hudaiba Soomro, Talise Oh, M. A. Eriksson, Benjamin D. Woods, Mark Friesen

item.title: Integrated optical isolators enabled by 2D semiconductors via spin-momentum locking
item.description: arXiv:2611.16125v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Integrated optical isolators based on spin-momentum locking hold great potential for protecting photonic integrated circuits from unwanted reflections. Currently, the most common implementations are magneto-optical isolators that require an externally applied magnetic field. Nevertheless, a wide range of nonreciprocal effects remains to be exploited in alternative material platforms. Although the majority of these effects induce changes to the propagation of light as a function of its polarization, they can be directly connected to the propagation direction through spin-momentum locking. We employ a computational approach to investigate various designs of integrated isolators based on nonreciprocal 2D semiconductors, studying the influence of their geometry and optical properties on the device performance. Additionally, we propose a novel concept for an all-optical isolator based on spin-valley polarization and optically tunable magnetism in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers. Our results establish 2D semiconductors as an advanced platform for integrated nonreciprocal devices, enabling functionalities that are difficult to achieve with conventional magneto-optical materials like all-optical operation.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Mart\'in-Romero, V\'ictor J. G\'omez, Alberto G. Curto

item.title: Intrinsic Chiral HOTI Stabilized by a Single Diagonal Reflection
item.description: arXiv:2611.16261v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Higher-order topological insulators and superconductors, under combined point and fundamental symmetries, display topological modes supported by boundaries of higher codimensions, such as a corner mode. In this work, we explain a theoretical device that enables us to claim that there exists {\it one and only one} intrinsic chiral-symmetric higher-order topological phase for the quarter-plane geometry with point-symmetry given by reflection about the diagonal of the corner. Furthermore, we supply a minimal tight-binding model of this phase and design an acoustic crystal whose dynamics reproduce that of the model. The robust properties of the corner mode are investigated by COMSOL simulations.
item.dc:creator: Danilo Polo Ojito, Jackson Saunders, Ellis Bender, Camelia Prodan, Emil Prodan

item.title: Quantum geometry drives orbital paramagnetism in superconducting fluctuations
item.description: arXiv:2611.16387v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Superconductors expel magnetic fields through the Meissner effect. Even slightly above the superconducting transition temperature, electrons can briefly form Cooper pairs, leading to an orbital diamagnetic susceptibility that diverges as the transition is approached. In this work, we use Gaussian fluctuation theory to study a generic multicomponent superconductor above its transition temperature and show that fluctuations can instead produce a paramagnetic response. We identify two competing contributions: the usual diamagnetic contribution from the center-of-mass motion of Cooper pairs and a paramagnetic contribution from interference between different components of the superconducting order parameter. The latter is related to pair quantum geometry, which describes how the internal components of the Cooper pair change with momentum. We then apply our theory to a model of a kagome superconductor with two chiral pairing modes. When the parent state preserves time-reversal symmetry, the paramagnetic contribution can outweigh the conventional diamagnetic contribution, producing net fluctuation paramagnetism. However, when the orbital time-reversal symmetry is broken, e.g., by forming a weak loop-current order, the degeneracy between the two chiral modes is then lifted. Upon cooling toward the superconducting transition, the lower-energy mode dominates the fluctuations, and diamagnetism wins as single-component physics takes over. Our results provide a mechanism for fluctuation paramagnetism in superconductors and show that the orbital magnetic response can probe the quantum geometry of Cooper pairs.
item.dc:creator: Zi-Ting Sun, Ying-Ming Xie, Chunli Huang, Naoto Nagaosa

item.title: Why "quantum spin liquids'' are quantum singlet liquids
item.description: arXiv:2611.16428v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The last couple of decades have seen enormous theoretical and experimental research efforts aimed at finding quantum spin liquids (QSLs) in geometrically frustrated (GF) magnetic materials. Experimental demonstrations of QSLs are challenging due to the indirect character of possible QSL signatures and the presence of impurities in materials, which may destroy or obscure a QSL. At the same time, theoretical literature often lacks consensus about the ground states of quantum spins on even the simplest GF magnetic lattices. We summarize experimental evidence that in the impurity-free limit, available GF magnetic materials that do not develop magnetic order at low temperatures would form {\it a quantum singlet liquid}, i.e. a disordered state of non-magnetic excitations. We further confirm the existence of such a singlet liquid and its gapless character with theoretical arguments. Such a liquid manifests itself in the thermodynamics of GF magnets while having no magnetic features at low temperatures.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Syzranov, Arthur P. Ramirez

item.title: Thermal Hall sign reversal from competing magnons and magnon pairs in pyrochlore spin-nematic magnets
item.description: arXiv:2611.16440v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bound magnon pairs are central to spin-nematic order, yet experimentally distinguishing them from single magnons remains challenging. We show that their Berry-curvature-driven heat transport provides a characteristic signature in the thermal Hall response. For a spin-$3/2$ pyrochlore antiferromagnet with ferromagnetic biquadratic exchange in the magnetic-field-induced fully polarized phase, we construct single-magnon bands together with magnon-pair bands, include the Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interaction, and evaluate their intrinsic thermal Hall conductivities. The lowest magnon and magnon-pair bands carry Berry curvatures of opposite sign. Because the gaps of the two quasiparticles respond differently to magnetic field, their competing contributions can drive both magnetic-field- and temperature-induced sign reversals of the thermal Hall conductivity. Estimates for chromium spinel oxides indicate that the effect can approach experimentally accessible magnitudes. We also find that the hybridization between the one- and two-magnon sectors induced by the DM interaction preserves this qualitative signature. These results suggest that a broad class of frustrated magnets with both magnons and magnon pairs provides a possible route to tuning the sign of the thermal Hall conductivity and probing bound magnon pairs through thermal transport experiments.
item.dc:creator: Tetsuya Sato, Emika Takata, Masahiro Sato

item.title: Noise-Protected Superconducting Qudits from Higher-Harmonic Josephson Junctions
item.description: arXiv:2611.16563v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Qudits, which generalize qubits to $d$ levels, store more information per circuit element than qubits. As with qubits, however, their sensitivity to noise must be overcome before they can be used for fault-tolerant quantum computing. Here we show that, by exploiting the second harmonic of the current--phase relation, a superconducting loop of three Josephson junctions can host qutrits strongly protected against relaxation, while dephasing limits their coherence. When the second harmonic is positive, a simple loop with a small asymmetry between the junctions provides a tunable, symmetry-protected qutrit. When it is negative, a protected qutrit can be realized by adding a small symmetry-breaking term, such as a weak Josephson diode effect. The two designs involve different trade-offs: the first has an exact charge selection rule, whereas the second is nearly insensitive to charge noise and its quasiparticle errors can be corrected. The preferable choice therefore depends on the materials used. Both require a sizable second harmonic to begin with, and we identify altermagnetic Josephson junctions as a candidate platform. Finally, microscopic calculations show that a gate voltage selects the sign of the second harmonic in these junctions, although gate-voltage noise then becomes the leading source of dephasing. These findings establish the sign of the second harmonic as a design principle for protected superconducting qudits.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Vakili

item.title: Gatemon qubits based on in-situ ternary InAsSb/Al nanowire Josephson junctions
item.description: arXiv:2611.16595v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ternary InAsSb/Al nanowires combine compositionally engineerable semiconductor properties with epitaxial proximity superconductivity, making them attractive for hybrid quantum circuits and mesoscopic superconductivity. Here, we realize gatemon qubits based on shadow-defined in-situ InAsSb/Al Josephson junctions in a single growth process. Gate-dependent microwave spectroscopy demonstrates electrostatic tuning of the qubit transition over several gigahertz. Rabi oscillations and Ramsey interference show coherent qubit control, with representative values T1 = 0.79 us and T2* = 0.91 us. Across five gatemons distributed over three chips, the measured relaxation times range from approximately 0.2 us to 1 us and decrease with increasing qubit frequency. Their magnitude is comparable to a circuit estimate of spontaneous emission into the electromagnetic environment. These results establish in-situ InAsSb/Al junctions as coherent, gate-tunable circuit elements and introduce cQED architecture as a microwave probe of the dynamics of the ternary weak link.
item.dc:creator: Zhenhai Sun, David Feldstein-Bofill, Sangeeth Kallatt, Sabbir A. Khan, Morten Kjaergaard

item.title: Detecting non-Hermitian topology from long-time dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.16745v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a protocol to measure the non-Hermitian topological invariant associated with the Lindbladian spectrum of chiral-symmetric open Gaussian systems from the relaxation of the covariance matrix. Importantly, the method works in the long-time regime and does not rely on isolating edge modes, so it remains applicable even when the Liouvillian skin effect may obscure them. We illustrate the technique on a Kitaev chain with reservoir-induced nonreciprocity, for which we first obtain a fully analytical and previously unknown description of its topological phase diagram. We then show that our protocol reliably distinguishes all the different phases.
item.dc:creator: Antonio D'Abbruzzo, Rosario Fazio

item.title: Asymmetric Frequency Conversion and Violation of Kirchhoff's Law of Thermal Radiation in Phased Floquet Metasurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.17062v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a system of three closely spaced conducting sheets, whose thermal emission largely violates Kirchhoff's law through nonreciprocal frequency conversion enabled by Floquet phenomena. We leverage surface mode transitions controlled by temporal modulation of one of the metasurfaces, resulting in largely asymmetric frequency conversion. Our findings broaden the capabilities of Floquet metasurfaces for wave conversion and energy manipulation, paving the way towards magnet-free nonreciprocal photonic devices with opportunities for thermal management and efficient photonic refrigeration.
item.dc:creator: Yao-Ting Wang, Emanuele Galiffi, Sander A. Mann, Mauro Antezza, Andrea Al\`u

item.title: Integer and Fractional Chern Plateaus Shaped by Layer-Dependent Disorder
item.description: arXiv:2611.17217v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The realization of integer and fractional Chern insulators in moir\'e systems provides a lattice setting for exploring how the structure of Bloch wave functions influences the interplay between topology and disorder. Here we investigate how layer-dependent disorder shapes Hall plateau widths and transitions. Using a realistic three-orbital model of twisted bilayer MoTe$_2$, we compare Hall and bulk transport under onsite-potential, displacement-field, and twist-angle disorder. At equal bare disorder strength, onsite-potential disorder produces broad integer plateaus with nearly direct transitions, whereas displacement-field disorder yields narrow plateaus separated by conducting regions with pronounced Hall-resistance dips. These contrasting behaviors arise from the layer composition of the Bloch states: contributions from different layer under displacement-field disorder partially cancel, weakening the bulk localization. Composite-fermion mean-field theory further yields fractional plateaus at $\nu_h=2/3$ and $3/5$ with the same disorder dependence of plateau widths. These findings identify layer-dependent disorder as an important mechanism shaping Chern plateau stability in moir\'e systems beyond bare disorder strength alone.
item.dc:creator: Ziyue Qi, Zhan Wang, Hongming Weng, Kun Jiang

item.title: Quantum Metrology and Quantum Battery in a Hyperfine-Coupled Spin System
item.description: arXiv:2611.17310v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate multiparameter quantum metrology and the energetic properties of an effective electron--proton spin system inspired by the hyperfine structure of the hydrogen atom. Considering the external magnetic field $\mathcal B$ and the hyperfine coupling strength $\Lambda$ as unknown parameters, we derive the quantum Fisher information matrix and establish the corresponding quantum Cram\'er--Rao bounds for their simultaneous estimation. We analyze the estimation precision and the correlations between the two parameters, showing that the weak-commutativity condition is satisfied despite the noncommutativity of the associated symmetric logarithmic derivatives. Independently, we explore the energetic properties of the system under a unitary charging protocol, characterizing its ergotropy, anti-ergotropy, storage capacity, and energy-basis coherence. We investigate the dependence of these quantities on the magnetic field, hyperfine coupling, temperature, and charging time. Our results provide a comprehensive characterization of the metrological properties and energetic performance of a hyperfine spin-based quantum system, highlighting its potential as a platform for quantum sensing and energy storage.
item.dc:creator: Omar Bachain, Mohamed Amazioug, Rachid Ahl Laamara

item.title: Probing tensor monopoles and gerbe invariants in three-dimensional topological matter
item.description: arXiv:2507.22116v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that momentum-space tensor monopoles corresponding to nontrivial vector bundle generalizations, known as bundle gerbes, can be realized in bands of three-dimensional topological matter with nontrivial Hopf invariants. We provide a universal construction of tensor Berry connections in these topological phases, demonstrating how obstructions therein lead to $\mathbb{Z}$-quantized bulk magnetoelectric and nonlinear optical phenomena in the presence of spacetime inversion ($\mathcal{PT}$) symmetry. We then pinpoint that these quantum effects are supported by intraband and interband torsion leading to nontrivial Dixmier-Douady classes in most known Hopf phases and in more general topological insulators realizing gerbe invariants falling beyond the tenfold classification of topological phases of matter. We furthermore provide an interacting generalization upon introducing many-body gerbe invariants by employing twisted boundary conditions. This opens an avenue to study gerbe invariants realized through higher-dimensional charge fractionalizations that can be electromagnetically probed.
item.dc:creator: Wojciech J. Jankowski, Robert-Jan Slager, Giandomenico Palumbo

item.title: Odd-Parity Altermagnetism Originating from Orbital Order
item.description: arXiv:2508.18361v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Odd-parity spin splitting plays a central role in spintronics and unconventional superconductivity, yet its microscopic realization in collinear magnetic systems remains elusive. We propose a general symmetry-based strategy for realizing odd-parity altermagnetism by stacking two noncentrosymmetric monolayers in an interlayer antiferromagnetic configuration. In this setting, odd-parity spin splitting originates from nonrelativistic complex orbital order rather than spin-orbit coupling. By exploiting lattice symmetries, our framework enables the realization of both $p$- and $f$-wave altermagnets with nontrivial topological properties. Depending on the symmetry principles governing the bilayer stacking, the resulting altermagnet can host either quantum spin Hall or Chern insulator phases. Our work expands the landscape of altermagnetic phases and opens new avenues for discovering fascinating physical phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Zheng-Yang Zhuang, Di Zhu, Dongling Liu, Zhigang Wu, Zhongbo Yan

item.title: Magnetocaloric effect for the altermagnetic candidate MnTe
item.description: arXiv:2510.02777v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We experimentally investigate magnetocaloric effect for single crystals of altermagnetic candidate MnTe at the transition to the state with spontaneous spin polarization, i.e. well below the N\'eel temperature of MnTe. The isothermal magnetic entropy change $\Delta S$ is calculated from the experimental magnetization curves by using Maxwell relation. We observe well-defined magnetocaloric effect as a narrow $\Delta S$ peak around the critical temperature $T_c\approx 81$~K, which reflects the sharp magnetization jump. This behavior is unusual for standard ferromagnetic transitions, so it confirms the predicted spin-orbit-induced spin polarization in the MnTe altermagnetic state and, therefore, confirms MnTe as a prototypical altermagnet candidate.
item.dc:creator: N. N. Orlova, V. D. Esin, A. V. Timonina, N. N. Kolesnikov, E. V. Deviatov

item.title: Manipulating anomalous transport via crystal symmetry in two-dimensional altermagnets
item.description: arXiv:2601.01564v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Anomalous transports, including the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) and anomalous Nernst effect (ANE), are typical manifestations of time-reversal-symmetry-breaking responses in materials. In general, the two Hall states with opposite Hall conductivities can be regarded as time-reversal pairs coupled to magnetic order, and switching between them relies on reversing the magnetization via an external magnetic field or electric current. Here, we introduce an approach for manipulating anomalous transport through crystal symmetry engineering in two-dimensional (2D) altermagnetic systems. Through symmetry analysis and lattice models, we show that for systems with out-of-plane N\'eel vectors, breaking the symmetry that connects two magnetic sublattices will induce an anomalous Hall response. Crucially, the signs of the anomalous Hall and anomalous Nernst conductivities can be flexibly controlled via symmetry-breaking perturbations, enabling the realizing tunable sign-reversible anomalous transport. Using first-principles calculations, we investigate crystal-symmetry-controlled anomalous transport in the 2D altermagnetic materials V$_{2}$STeO and Cr$_{2}$O$_{2}$. The results indicate that these systems with out-of-plane N\'eel vectors exhibit pronounced AHE and ANE signals under uniaxial strain. Remarkably, the sign of the anomalous transport coefficients can be reversed by simply rotating the strain direction by $\pi/2$, thus enabling the switching of anomalous transverse currents without an external magnetic field. Our findings provide a new strategy to manipulate anomalous transport, and should have significant potential applications.
item.dc:creator: Dan Li, Shuaiyu Wang, Jiabin chen, Zeling Li, Chaoxi Cui, Lei Li, Lei Wang, Zhi-Ming Yu, Xiaodong Zhou, Xiao-Ping Li

item.title: Magnon equilibrium spin current in collinear antiferromagnets
item.description: arXiv:2601.16184v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We theoretically predict that the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction can induce a magnon equilibrium spin current in collinear antiferromagnets. Such a current, being a response to the effective magnon vector potential, can be considered the magnon analog of the supercurrent in superconductors. The large amplitude of the predicted effect may compensate for the smallness of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, making the equilibrium spin currents experimentally observable. Importantly, we show that the current being the ground state property isn't zero at zero temperature. We suggest that an external electric field can play the role of an effective flux that magnons interact with, and we propose an experiment based on the interference of magnons in a ring geometry to verify the concept.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir A. Zyuzin

item.title: Quasi-1D Planar Magnetic Topological Heterostructure
item.description: arXiv:2604.01823v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We theoretically introduce a quasi one dimensional magnetic heterostructure of alternating 2D topological and normal insulator strips. Such a structure can be realized by special fabrication techniques or may emerge naturally in twisted bilayers of certain transition metal dichalcogenides. Its low-energy physics is governed by a hybrid Hamiltonian intertwining the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger and Shockley models, with spin-momentum locking and local Zeeman splitting. Symmetry analysis places it in class AIII, characterized by chiral symmetry and a $\mathbb{Z}$ topological invariant. Computing the winding number from the block-off-diagonal structure of the Hamiltonian reveals topological phases characterized by invariants $\nu = 0$, $1$, and $2$. Furthermore, a single magnetic defect acts as a sensitive local probe, whose in-gap spectrum provides a spectroscopic fingerprint to distinguish global topological phases. We show that the frequency-dependent optical absorption induced by such a defect exhibits distinct features in the topological and trivial phases, offering an independent, experimentally accessible local indicator of the global topological order. Extending the platform to a multilayer geometry uncovers a nonsymmorphic projective symmetry that gives rise to M\"obius band topology.
item.dc:creator: Z. Z. Alisultanov

item.title: Hidden Quantum-Geometric Connection between Injection and Shift Currents
item.description: arXiv:2605.08643v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Injection current (IC) and shift current (SC) are generally regarded as distinct nonlinear optical responses with different microscopic origins. Here, within the clean limit, based on an independent-particle interband description, we uncover a general hidden connection between the IC and SC responses. The generalized-derivative sum rule is used to show that the SC response separates into an injection-determined contribution associated with velocity asymmetry and a genuine shift-current (GSC) contribution associated with real-space wave-packet displacement. In systems with approximately linear electronic dispersion near the Fermi level, the corresponding tensor combinations of SC and IC can become effectively equivalent at low photon energies, governed by the same interband quantum-geometric dipole. Crystal symmetry can also eliminate the injection-determined contribution, enabling direct access to the GSC component. Extending our approach to second-harmonic generation reveals analogous response relations, suggesting a route toward a broader network of quantitative connections among the various nonlinear optical responses.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Yahyavi, Tay-Rong Chang, Md Shafayat Hossain, Arun Bansil, Naoto Nagaosa, Guoqing Chang

item.title: Magneto-optical signal from $\mathrm{Co_2Mn}$-based Heusler thin films in MOKE and BLS
item.description: arXiv:2608.07052v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: $\mathrm{Co_2Mn}$-based Heusler compounds offer a versatile, composition-tunable platform for magnonics and spintronics. Among them, the half-metallic $\mathrm{Co_2MnSi}$ is of particular interest for magnonics owing to its ultralow Gilbert damping, yet its weak magneto-optical response in the visible challenges optical probing such as Brillouin light scattering (BLS). We study the magneto-optical response of epitaxial $\mathrm{Co_2Mn}X$ films ($X = \{\mathrm{Al}_x\mathrm{Si}_{1-x}, \mathrm{Ga}_x\mathrm{Ge}_{1-x}, \mathrm{Sn}\}$) by magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) spectroscopy and BLS. Angle-resolved MOKE resolves a significant, wavelength-dependent quadratic MOKE (QMOKE) only for $\mathrm{Co_2MnSi}$, whereas $\mathrm{Co_2MnAl}$, $\mathrm{Co_2MnGa}$ and $\mathrm{Co_2MnSn}$ respond dominantly linearly. Comparing BLS intensities of thermal magnons at two wavelengths, $\mathrm{Co_2MnSi}$ gives the weakest signal at 532 nm yet among the strongest at 457 nm, tracking the spectral dependence of its Kerr angle. These results emphasise the relation between the two magneto-optical techniques, guiding the choice of probing wavelength for $\mathrm{Co_2Mn}$-based Heusler compounds, and provide a transferable approach for other magnetic materials.
item.dc:creator: Anna Maria Friedel, Nicolas Fermon, Tobias B\"ottcher, S\'ebastien Petit-Watelot, St\'ephane Andrieu, Philipp Pirro

item.title: Fubini-Study Speed and Short-Time Identification of Bosonic Instability
item.description: arXiv:2608.12406v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We ask what short-time quantum distinguishability reveals about instability in quadratic bosonic systems. For a fixed autonomous quadratic Hamiltonian, the infimum of the Fubini-Study speed over centered pure Gaussian inputs equals the Euclidean norm of the positive real parts of the flow eigenvalues divided by the square root of 2. The infimum is attained exactly when the flow generator is diagonalizable. We also derive the minimum speed under a finite squeezing budget for a detuned parametric amplifier. For a lossy single-mode amplifier with a common phase-insensitive Markovian bath, two return-fidelity traces, from the bare vacuum and a calibrated squeezed vacuum, determine the growth margin, damping, and diffusion from their initial slopes and curvatures. Finite-window simulations illustrate how the traces distinguish cases on opposite sides of the instability threshold.
item.dc:creator: A. M. Tishin

item.title: Topologically protected zero-reflection nodes for perfect crossed Andreev reflection
item.description: arXiv:2608.26702v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Generating non-locally entangled electron pairs via Cooper-pair splitting is vital for solid-state quantum information processing. However, isolating the underlying crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) is challenging due to competing transport processes like electron tunneling (ET) and local Andreev reflection (AR). Here, we propose a flux-tunable four-terminal normal metal-superconductor junction that achieves deterministic, 100\% efficient CAR. We demonstrate that at exactly half a magnetic flux quantum ($\phi=\pi$), exact destructive Aharonov-Bohm and Peierls interferences structurally forbid ET and AR, respectively. By tuning the central junction hopping, electron reflection is also suppressed to zero. Using the Cauchy argument principle, we prove that this zero-reflection node is topologically protected by a quantized winding number in parameter space. When combined with the precise spatial symmetries of the junction, this exact suppression guarantees a unit CAR probability. We establish that this regime is characterized by a strictly positive cross-correlation shot noise, providing an unambiguous experimental signature of Cooper-pair splitting. Furthermore, this perfect CAR is nearly broadband within the superconducting gap. While generic structural disorder breaks the spatial symmetries required for the exact cancellation of ET and AR, the crossed Andreev reflection--though no longer perfectly quantized --remains highly dominant under weak disorder, offering a resilient architecture for deterministic nonlocal entanglement generation.
item.dc:creator: Abhiram Soori

item.title: Magnetic Quadrupole Lens and Current-Induced Quadrupolar Dynamics of Antiskyrmion
item.description: arXiv:2609.23129v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We demonstrate that antiskyrmions can serve as magnetic quadrupole lenses that focus or defocus electric currents traversing them. We showcase the antiskyrmion core as a focal point where electron beams converge for specific injection directions, leading to anisotropic and nonuniform current distributions. Thus the current-induced antiskyrmion dynamics is profoundly modified by the magnetic quadrupole lensing via the spin-transfer torque. By incorporating quantum transport and micromagnetic simulations iteratively, we self-consistently capture the coupled dynamics of conduction electrons and antiskyrmions. Our results unveil a quadrupolar antiskyrmion Hall effect that is highly anisotropic with respect to the current direction and can be effectively tuned by the spin-orbit coupling. In particular, the current focusing (defocusing) dramatically enhances (suppresses) the antiskyrmion speed while simultaneously reducing its Hall angle, thereby overcoming a key challenge for antiskyrmion racetrack memories. Our work establishes the intrinsic current lensing as a powerful mechanism for manipulating topological magnetic textures and opens new avenues for antiskyrmion-based spintronics.
item.dc:creator: Linfeng Du, Yang Liu, Peng Yan, Ying Su

item.title: Intrinsic spin-orbit coupling in graphene stacks
item.description: arXiv:2610.05905v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The effect of spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in monolayer graphene has been thoroughly studied in the past. Its impact is commonly disregarded since the electronic structure of graphene is almost unaffected. Consequently, SOC has also been ignored in other graphitic systems. In this work, we calculate the intrinsic SOC in stacks of graphene layers from a model that includes all the valence orbitals of carbon as well as the intra-atomic SOC.The leading spin-orbit term in a graphene multilayer combines a Rashba-like spin-flip process with interlayer hopping. We find that this intrinsic term modifies the phase diagram and Fermi surfaces of finite rhombohedral stacks, and it leads to a distinct density-dependence of the magnetization in weak magnetic fields. This Letter shows that, unlike in the single-layer case, SOC has important consequences in multilayer graphitic systems and it should not be neglected when studying their physical properties.
item.dc:creator: Guillermo Parra-Martinez, Alejandro Jimeno-Pozo, Ady Stern, Jose Angel Silva-Guill\'en, Francisco Guinea

item.title: Nodal magnon spin current at an antiferromagnet/altermagnet junction
item.description: arXiv:2610.39206v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the thermally driven magnon spin current across a junction between a $d$-wave altermagnet (AM) and a ferromagnet (FM) or an antiferromagnet (AFM). The current consists of a component independent of the interface angle and an angularly dependent component with the $d$-wave form. For a sublattice-symmetric interface, the two junctions behave oppositely under reversal of the altermagnetic domain: in the FM/AM junction the angularly dependent component is odd and cancels on averaging over the domains, whereas in the AFM/AM junction the angularly independent component vanishes by symmetry and the angularly dependent component survives the domain average at a fixed N\'eel vector of the AFM. Both follow from a selective tunneling: a pair of spins bonded across the interface transmits magnons when the spins are parallel and not when antiparallel, which makes the AFM/AM junction a magnon valve: the configuration in which the bonded spins are antiparallel blocks the current up to the sublattice admixture of the magnons. We reveal the uniqueness of the altermagnet by comparing with the anisotropic antiferromagnet. The anisotropic tunneling is detectable as the sign reversal of the current between the interfaces normal to $[310]$ and $[130]$, and the valve reads the N\'eel vector of the altermagnet relative to that of the antiferromagnet through the magnitude of the current at a fixed interface.
item.dc:creator: Koki Mizuno

item.title: Influence of pairing and correlations on transport properties in three-terminal superconducting nanostructure
item.description: arXiv:2610.40059v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the local and nonlocal charge transport properties of three-terminal nanostructure, consisting of the correlated quantum dot embedded between two metallic electrodes and superconductor. Using the linear response theory, we analyze interplay of the induced on-dot pairing with the correlation effects, inspecting their influence on the conductance and thermopower. Our calculations predict negative values of the nonlocal conductance and reversal of the Seebeck coefficient when the quantum dot ground state is represented by the BCS-type singlet configuration. These phenomena are realized when the subgap charge transport is predominantly contributed by the crossed Andreev scattering. In contrast, on the doublet side, we obtain signatures for the Kondo effect manifested by the low-temperature enhancement of the charge conductance and clearly evident in the thermopower. Such temperature-dependent local and nonlocal transport properties can unambiguously identify the specific configuration of the correlated quantum dot and reveal the rich physics emerging in the doublet-to-singlet crossover region.
item.dc:creator: G. G\'orski, V. Pokorn\'y, T. Doma\'nski

item.title: Prediction of antimagnon-polarons with intrinsic momentum-space level attraction
item.description: arXiv:2611.07434v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Propagating hybrid quasiparticles formed by magnons and phonons (magnon-polarons) or photons (magnon-polaritons) typically exhibit level repulsion in momentum space. Level attraction, by contrast, requires an anti-phase channel and has so far been restricted to zero-dimensional systems mediated by dissipative baths. Here we predict the antimagnon-polaron in a continuous magnetoelastic medium, which inherently exhibits momentum-space level attraction. The spin-orbit-torque (SOT)-stabilized antimagnon precesses with opposite handedness, directly reversing the magnetoelastic coupling without requiring an external environment. This intrinsic attraction yields a distinctive 0/{\pi} phase-locked simultaneous growth. Micromagnetic simulations confirm this picture, revealing that the SOT-controlled balance between gain and damping drives a collective instability. This ultimately enables a continuously tunable, dc-pumped, single-frequency phonon laser, establishing a novel route for coherent acoustic emission.
item.dc:creator: Chongzhou Wang, Zhengda Jing, Weichao Yu

item.title: Enhancing valley splitting in Si/SiGe Wiggle Well quantum dots through integrated stressor-gate architectures
item.description: arXiv:2611.12850v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Engineering large and reproducible valley splittings is essential for the scalable operation of silicon spin qubits. In Si/SiGe quantum dot devices, valley splitting arises predominantly from atomic-scale disorder and is therefore inherently random, motivating approaches that introduce a large deterministic contribution. Strain-assisted Wiggle Wells provide a route to deterministic valley splitting by combining an oscillatory Ge concentration in the Si well with shear strain; however, generating the required strain in a manner compatible with large-scale architectures remains a challenge. Here, we propose patterned stressed thin films as a scalable approach for generating shear strain in the quantum well of Si/SiGe quantum dot devices. Finite-element simulations show that compressively stressed TiN films can generate shear strains exceeding 0.1% at the quantum well, sufficient for deterministic valley splittings of hundreds of $\mu \text{eV}$ in strain-assisted Wiggle Wells. We show that this strain can extend across multiple quantum dots and is maintained in realistic gate geometries, providing a fabrication-compatible approach for scaling deterministic valley splitting to quantum dot arrays.
item.dc:creator: E. S. Joseph, Talise Oh, D. E. Savage, D. S. Stone, DeAnna Campbell, Benjamin D. Woods, Mark Friesen, M. A. Eriksson

item.title: Geometry-Selective Higher-order topological insulators induced by $d_{xy}$ altermagnet
item.description: arXiv:2611.13438v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that proximity to a $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnet provides an effective route to engineering boundary-geometry-dependent higher-order topological phases. The boundary geometry plays a crucial role in determining the topological properties: axis-aligned edge states remain gapless, whereas diagonal edges acquire effective masses with alternating signs, giving rise to four corner modes localized at the mass domain walls. By projecting onto the edge-state subspace, we derive the effective edge Hamiltonians for different boundary geometries. Furthermore, $\pi$-flux defects introduced under periodic boundary conditions yield zero-energy bound states localized at the flux cores, providing complementary evidence for nontrivial topology without physical boundaries. The interplay between the Zeeman field and the altermagnetic order drives a topological transition through the closing and reopening of the edge gap, while the bulk gap remains open. These findings highlight the crucial role of boundary geometry in higher-order topology and establish proximity-induced $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnetism as a route to engineering higher-order topological phases.
item.dc:creator: Siyuan Cheng, Yuee Xie, Xiaosen Yang, Yuanping Chen

item.title: Edge quantum weight of finite Chern flakes and its topological floor
item.description: arXiv:2611.14271v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The zero-point energy of an $LC$ circuit measures the polarization fluctuation of an insulator coupled to it. In a crystal this fluctuation is the bulk quantum weight $K_{\rm bulk}$, which the Chern number $C$ bounds below by $|C|$. We show that a finite Chern flake adds an edge term that survives as the flake grows. The low-frequency transitions of its chiral edge have squared dipole matrix elements that sum to an edge weight $K_{\rm edge}\ge |C|$ per unit area, a floor that follows from the positive absorption of both circular polarizations and the known cancellation of circular dichroism between edge and bulk. At weak coupling, which a growing flake eventually leaves, a circuit slower than the edge modes reads $K_{\rm bulk}+K_{\rm edge}$, averaged over two field directions, and a faster one approaches $K_{\rm bulk}$, so the reading depends on whether the flake is made large or the circuit slow first. In exact free-fermion calculations on lattice flakes with $|C|=1$ and 2 the summed circular dichroism of the edge sector extrapolates to $|C|$ in magnitude, so that the floor is $|C|$. Above the floor, each edge channel adds a number fixed by the boundary shape and its edge velocities, which square and rectangular lattice flakes with one channel follow to within 0.003, while the circular dichroism counts only the net chirality. The avoided crossing of the circuit with the edge mode gives the edge weight in units of the Hall conductance quantum, up to a geometric factor of the capacitor.
item.dc:creator: Rohit Narula

item.title: High-frequency dispersive readout of a superconducting qubit
item.description: arXiv:2501.09161v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Driving a low-dissipation, non-linear system periodically can destabilize it by exciting indirect resonances, which occur whenever an integer multiple of the drive frequency matches an integer combination of the system's mode frequencies. Avoiding such resonances is a central design constraint across physics and engineering, from radio-frequency ion traps to particle accelerators. Remarkably, the measurement of quantum bits based on superconducting circuits has so far remained limited by non-linear resonances. Measurements of qubit states are customarily performed in a regime where the frequency of the microwave readout tone is comparable to that of the circuit. In that case, the drive excites resonances that eject the qubit from its computational subspace. This limits the readout power and hence the achievable measurement fidelity. We show that a readout tone with frequency much larger than that of the circuit circumvents this problem by exponentially suppressing the resonances. Using a readout tone with frequency 12 times larger than that of our transmon qubit, we achieve a quantum non-demolition measurement fidelity of $99.931\pm0.003\%$, with an error an order of magnitude smaller than the previous record. Under these conditions, the probability of leakage to non-computational states per readout is $0.018\pm0.002\%$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel D. Kurilovich, Thomas Connolly, Charlotte G. L. B{\o}ttcher, Daniel K. Weiss, Sumeru Hazra, Vidul R. Joshi, Andy Z. Ding, Heekun Nho, Spencer Diamond, Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Mykola Kishmar, Wei Dai, Valla Fatemi, Luigi Frunzio, Leonid I. Glazman, Michel H. Devoret

item.title: Resolving the Quantum Origin of Anisotropic Raman Response in Quasi-1D $Ta_2$$Ni_3$$Te_5$
item.description: arXiv:2506.05809v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Probing anisotropic electron-phonon interactions (EPIs) is fundamental to understanding low-dimensional quantum materials, yet isolating their intrinsic signatures remains a challenge due to the confounding influence of extrinsic effects. Here, we resolve this ambiguity in quasi-one-dimensional $Ta_2$$Ni_3$$Te_5$ through a combination of angle-resolved polarized Raman spectroscopy and density functional perturbation theory (DFPT). Anomalous four-lobe angular dependences were observed in Ag phonon modes, which deviate from the real-valued Raman tensor prediction. Further, we explicitly highlight that, despite their distinct physical origins, light absorption and birefringence yield mathematically identical angular dependencies in $Ta_2$$Ni_3$$Te_5$, rendering phenomenological fitting alone insufficient to identify the true physical mechanism. By employing a full quantum treatment incorporating detailed interaction mechanisms, we capture the qualitative characteristics and mode-to-mode diversity of the anomalous angular responses observed experimentally. The DFPT calculations further reveal mode-specific and momentum-resolved EPIs, providing microscopic support for anisotropic EPIs as the mechanism of anomalous Raman responses.
item.dc:creator: Fei Wang, Qiaohui Zhou, Hong Tang, Fan Zhang, Yanxing Li, Steven A. Hindmarsh, Chengkun Xing, Keyuan Bai, Sidra Younus, Ana M. Sanchez, Haidong Zhou, Chih-Kang Shih, Adrienn Ruzsinszky, Xin Lu, Jiang Wei

item.title: Evidence for time-reversal symmetry breaking and glassy dynamics in superconducting (La,Pr,Sm)3Ni2O7 films
item.description: arXiv:2508.16412v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Superconductivity and magnetism are generally distinct and competing orders, characterized by different broken symmetries and order parameters. Although they may coexist in some correlated systems, whether and how these orders can become inherently intertwined in unconventional high-transition-temperature (high-Tc) superconductors remains a central open question. Here, we report time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking and glassy dynamics in the superconducting state of nickelate (La,Pr,Sm)3Ni2O7 films. Magnetoresistance hysteresis and zero-field non-reciprocal charge transport, complementary evidence for broken TRS, are observed in the superconducting state, while absent in the normal state. Within the superconducting transition regime, logarithmically slow resistance relaxations following magnetic-field perturbations provide strong evidence for glassy dynamics. Remarkably, the reproducible temperature hierarchy across multiple films reveals that these novel phenomena emerge concurrently with developing superconducting phase coherence, preceding the zero-resistance state. Consistently, scanning superconducting quantum interference device (sSQUID) microscopy directly resolves the zero-field magnetic-flux patterns indicative of spontaneous TRS breaking, which emerge simultaneously with local superconducting diamagnetism and phase stiffness. Our observations suggest a frustrated multicomponent superconducting order parameter in the nickelate films, whose internal relative phases may carry TRS-breaking chirality and freeze into a textured phase glass. Collectively, our findings identify a distinctive form of superconductivity in which internal phase degrees of freedom may support additional broken symmetries and glassy order, offering a new perspective on intertwined ordering phenomena in unconventional high-Tc superconductors.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Ji, Zheyuan Xie, Yaqi Chen, Guangdi Zhou, Keyi Liang, Rui Liu, Mengqiao Geng, Meixuan Li, Longxin Pan, Heng Wang, Haoliang Huang, Jun Ge, Yi Liu, Yang Liu, Guang-Ming Zhang, Yihua Wang, Ziqiang Wang, Qi-Kun Xue, Zhuoyu Chen, Jian Wang

item.title: Decoherence and the Reemergence of Coherence From a Superconducting "Horizon"
item.description: arXiv:2603.16765v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In a recent paper [arXiv:2205.06279], Danielson et al. demonstrated that the mere presence of a black hole causes universal decoherence of quantum superpositions (dubbed the DSW decoherence). We analyze decoherence in a superconducting analogue [arXiv:1709.06154] of the event horizon of a late-stage black hole, where Andreev reflection plays the role of Hawking radiation. We consider a normal metal interferometer threaded by an Aharonov-Bohm flux, where one of the arms of the interferometer is coupled to a superconductor by a tunnel coupling of varying strength. At absolute zero temperature and for weak coupling, we find that the scattering states of the interferometer are decohered by Andreev reflection, a nontrivial manifestation of the proximity effect analogous to DSW decoherence from the event horizon of a black hole. However, for increasing coupling strength to the superconductor, we find a reemergence of coherence via resonant tunneling through Andreev bound states. This suggests the existence of an analogue gravitational phenomenon wherein transmission mediated by virtual Hawking radiation leads to a reemergence of coherence in an interferometer placed near a black hole's event horizon.
item.dc:creator: Eric J. Sung, Charles A. Stafford

item.title: Tuning of quantum nanoscaled friction within the Prandtl-Tomlinson model
item.description: arXiv:2604.27216v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Nanoscaled is a fundamental tribological phenomenon with complex behavior of its dynamical force. Here, we utilize the Prandtl-Tomlinson framework to investigate systematically the different means of control of the frictional force at the quantum and classical levels. It is found that the frictional dynamics can be controlled by the corrugation and characteristic length ratio parameters dependent upon properties of the nanoparticle-chain system. In addition to the stick-slip regime, other types of motion are uncovered, highlighting the richness of the frictional dynamics. The importance of Landau-Zener tunneling for the quantum motion is also analyzed. These findings provide valuable insights for interpreting experimental observations and controlling quantum frictional behavior in nanoscale systems.
item.dc:creator: Dai-Nam Le, Lilia M. Woods

item.title: Identifiability and endpoint reconstruction of time-dependent Jacobi Hamiltonians from projective trajectory jets
item.description: arXiv:2605.22796v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the identifiability of smooth time-dependent Jacobi Hamiltonians from phase-resolved Schrodinger trajectories. When the initial state is localized at a chain endpoint, we prove that the projective trajectory jet through order M+1 uniquely determines the first M couplings, their logarithmic time derivatives, and the associated diagonal energy differences at preparation. This derivative order is necessary in the unrestricted real-Jacobi class. If only the first K projective coordinates are observed, even their full Taylor jets leave every deeper instantaneous layer undetermined. We also construct evolutions that are indistinguishable on an observation window separated from preparation but have different endpoint coupling scales and rates. We identify two ways to restore local identifiability: first-order projective and reference-population data at generic times, or second-order data from ceil(M/2) suitable site preparations for independent coupling rates. Statistical distinguishability bounds and finite-window simulations quantify the effects of noise, nuisance coefficients, and acquisition design.
item.dc:creator: A. M. Tishin

item.title: High-purity entanglement mediated by magnons despite weak coupling
item.description: arXiv:2607.19533v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Entangling distant spins via a shared magnonic bus typically faces a tradeoff: stronger spin-magnon coupling increases the entanglement fidelity, but also the spin decay rate. We propose a protocol that breaks this tradeoff. The magnons couple only to a transition outside the computational basis, in which the Bell state is created. Our protocol is probabilistic, and weak coupling reduces the success probability but not the fidelity. We analyze a setup where the spins are two nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers near a magnetic wire. In the absence of NV dephasing, the protocol reaches unit fidelity with a maximally entangled state, for arbitrarily weak coupling. In our simulations via the Monte-Carlo wavefunction approach, the NV-magnon coupling is taken to be one-third of the magnon linewidth. Considering finite NV dephasing, we predict a fidelity of >0.99 for a state-of-the-art rate, and an optimal fidelity of 0.91 for a moderate rate, both at 0.6% success probability.
item.dc:creator: Sanchar Sharma

item.title: Two-photon interference from as-grown InAsP/InP quantum dots under detuned excitation
item.description: arXiv:2607.26957v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this study, we investigate as-grown InAsP/InP quantum dots emitting in the third telecommunication window. The investigated quantum dots are embedded directly in an aluminium-free InP matrix without additional barrier material. A large excitation-emission detuning of 32 meV enables efficient suppression of scattered laser light while retaining several advantages of near-resonant excitation. The single-photon nature of the emission is confirmed by a Hanbury Brown and Twiss experiment, yielding a raw second-order autocorrelation value of $g_{\mathrm{raw}}^{(2)}(0)=0.076(6)$. A Hong-Ou-Mandel measurement is used to determine the degree of indistinguishability of single photons and reveals as-measured visibilities of $V=0.038(8)$ and $V=0.108(18)$ for excitation pulse separations of 13.1 ns and 5.3 ns, respectively. We observe finite photon indistinguishability in as-grown InAsP/InP quantum dots under detuned quasi-resonant excitation, without deliberate Purcell enhancement.
item.dc:creator: Maja Wasiluk, Anna Musia{\l}, Pawe{\l} Mrowi\'nski, Johann Peter Reithmaier, Mohamed Benyoucef, Wojciech Rudno-Rudzi\'nski

item.title: Collective photon echoes in the Tavis-Cummings model: distribution independence, two detuning regimes, and the Dicke ladder
item.description: arXiv:2608.21442v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An ensemble of $N$ two-level molecules prepared in its ground state and sharing a lossless cavity with a weak field does not simply absorb: the intensity collapses and then recurs, in a train of collective photon echoes. Working from the exact solution of the Tavis-Cummings model in the few-photon regime $\bar n<N$, we confirm the echo time $\tau_E=4\pi\sqrt{N+\Delta}/g$ at resonance from $N=5$ to $N=400$, and separate it from the alternative $4\pi\sqrt{N-\bar n+\Delta}/g$ by a direct test: the recurrence period is independent of $\bar n$ to $0.8\%$ across a factor of six in $\bar n$, where the alternative predicts shifts of up to $17\%$. The initial state, the ground state, requires no preparation. The echo time is independent of the initial photon distribution - coherent, thermal, squeezed and oscillatory-squeezed distributions with variances from 2 to 34 all recur together - but the echo amplitude is not: it varies at the tens-of-percent level at fixed mean, including a factor of 1.8 with the squeezing phase. Detuning organizes the dynamics into two clean regimes separated by a fragmented crossover; the echo time in the dispersive branch is exactly one-half that of the resonant branch, a factor derived from second-order dispersive perturbation theory with leading correction $5Ng^2/\delta^2$, and sufficient detuning removes the dependence on the initial Dicke state. For arbitrary initial $|r=N/2,m\rangle$, emission replaces absorption at $m\simeq-N/2+\bar n$, and the echo envelope acquires one component per step up the ladder. Lindblad simulations with all loss channels acting simultaneously, and full-Hilbert-space disorder simulations, show the first echoes to be observable at $N\sim5$-$20$ on an existing five-qubit superconducting device: the echo survives cavity decay with contrast $\sim e^{-\kappa\tau_E/2}$, photons being shielded while resident in the emitters.
item.dc:creator: Michael Tavis

item.title: Field-free precessional magnetization dynamics in a multidomain magnet driven by light-induced strain
item.description: arXiv:2608.29245v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ultrafast lattice excitation offers a route to controlling magnetization through magnetoelastic coupling, yet its ability to drive large-amplitude dynamics within pre-existing multidomain states remains less explored. Here, we show that a single 5-ps mid-infrared pulse induces a large-amplitude, reversible magnetic response in cobalt-doped yttrium iron garnet at zero applied magnetic field. Time-resolved magneto-optical microscopy reveals a transient reversal of the out-of-plane magnetic contrast within approximately 2 ns, followed by recovery of the initial state, while the labyrinthine domain morphology remains largely preserved. Concurrent polarization microscopy reveals a localized, long-lived strain-sensitive response and a propagating acoustic wave. The correlated structural and magnetic responses, together with micromagnetic simulations, support a mechanism in which transient strain modifies the magnetic anisotropy and drives precessional reorientation within existing domains. These findings establish single-pulse magnetoelastic excitation as a route to reversible, large-amplitude magnetization dynamics without substantial domain reorganization or an externally applied magnetic field.
item.dc:creator: H\'elo\"ise Damas, Carl S. Davies, Tomasz Zalewski, Petr M. Vetoshko, Vladimir I. Belotelov, Andrzej Stupakiewicz, Andrei Kirilyuk

item.title: SHAPE: a sparse Hamiltonian approach for prescribing eigenstates in metamaterials
item.description: arXiv:2610.37248v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Metamaterials, which store, guide and emit waves through their eigenstates, have enabled the development of devices with diverse functionalities. Yet the spatial profiles of conventional metamaterials' eigenstates are typically determined by their pre-determined structures (Hamiltonians). Here we develop SHAPE, a sparse Hamiltonian approach that enables the realization of prescribed, spectrally isolated eigenstates in physically realizable metamaterials. The resulting Hamiltonian geometries obey a boundary law, with the required nonlocality determined solely by single-contact boundary sites ($|E_{\mathrm{LR}}| = |\partial\Omega|$), independent of the state interior or lattice size. The Hamiltonians are further spectrally reshaped to open a protective gap around the target eigenstate. We validate our approach in discrete lattices and acoustic metamaterials. We provide a database of over 100 target states and a customizable design program, demonstrating the generality and extensibility of our method. Although demonstrated in acoustics, the principle can be applied to thermal, electrical-circuit and photonic metamaterials.
item.dc:creator: Yutao Chen, Tao Xiao, Jing Li, Aodong Li, Biye Xie
